arxiv-2110-03131.title: Universal relation for supernova gravitational waves
arxiv-2110-03131.creator: Hajime Sotani, Tomoya Takiwaki, Hajime Togashi
arxiv-2110-03131.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hajime Sotani, Tomoya Takiwaki, Hajime Togashi. Using the numerical simulation data for two-dimensional core-collapse supernova, we examine the protoneutron star (PNS) asteroseismology with the relativistic Cowling approximation. As shown in the previous study, the gravitational wave signals appearing in the numerical simulation can be well identified with the gravity (fundamental) oscillation in the early (later) phase before (after) the avoided crossing between the gravity and fundamental oscillations.

arxiv-2408-10674.creator: Henrique Gomes, Tushar Menon
arxiv-2408-10674.description: Abstract We show that the geometric structure of an arbitrary relativistic spacetime can be determined by the transformation groups associated with a collection of privileged coordinate systems. oliver.pooley@philosophy.ox.ac.uk james.read@philosophy.ox.ac.uk 1 Introduction Can the geometric structure of an arbitrary relativistic spacetime be presented via a collection of privileged coordinate systems?

arxiv-2502-04360.title: MARAGE: Transferable Multi-Model Adversarial Attack for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Data Extraction
arxiv-2502-04360.creator: Xiao Hu Eric Liu Weizhou Wang Xiangyu Guo David Lie
arxiv-2502-04360.description: Abstract Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) offers a solution to mitigate hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) by grounding their outputs to knowledge retrieved from external sources. The use of private resources and data in constructing these external data stores can expose them to risks of extraction attacks, in which attackers attempt to steal data from these private databases.

arxiv-2504-07433.description: Abstract The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has significantly promoted the development of code generation task, sparking a surge in pertinent literature. arxiv-2509-18902.title: Teaching RDM in a smart advanced inorganic lab course and its provision in the DALIA platform
arxiv-2509-18902.creator: Alexander Hoffmann, Jochen Ortmeyer, Fabian Fink, Charles Tapley Hoyt, Jonathan D. Geiger, Paul Kehrein, Torsten Schrade, Sonja Herres-Pawlis
arxiv-2509-18902.description: Abstract Research data management (RDM) is a key data literacy skill that chemistry students must acquire. Concepts such as the FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) should be taught and applied in undergraduate studies already. Traditionally, research data from labs, theses, and internships were handwritten and stored in inaccessible formats such as PDFs, limiting reuse and machine learning applications.

arxiv-2509-23481.title: Dipolar electroweak properties of Dirac massive neutrinos
arxiv-2509-23481.creator: J. P. Gutiérrez-Montes 1 , J. Montaño-Domínguez 1,2 , F. Ramírez-Zavaleta 1 , E. S. Tututi 1 and O. Vázquez-Hernández 1,2
arxiv-2509-23481.description: Abstract Electroweak properties of Dirac neutrinos within the context of the Minimally Extended Standard Model are explored. In particular, the dipolar form factors that result from the radiative correction, at one-loop level, of the Z ​ ν ​ ν ¯ Z\nu\bar{\nu} coupling are identified. The calculation is carried out in the covariant general gauge R ξ R_{\xi} .

pmc-10560230.title: ceRNA network-regulated COL1A2 high expression correlates with poor prognosis and immune infiltration in colon adenocarcinoma
pmc-10560230.creator: Xia Yuan, Yi He, Wei Wang
pmc-10560230.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Collagen type I α 2 (COL1A2) is a major component of collagen type I. Recently, abnormal COL1A2 expression has been reported in human cancers. However, the specific role and mechanism of COL1A2 in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) remain unclear. We performed the pan-cancer analysis of COL1A2 expression in 33 types of human cancers from TIMER database and integrated data combined TCGA with GTEx. The prognostic values of COL1A2 for 17 cancer types of interest were estimated from GEPIA database.

pmc-10642370.title: Arginine reprograms metabolism in liver cancer via RBM39
pmc-10642370.creator: Dirk Mossmann, Christoph Müller, Sujin Park, Brendan Ryback, Marco Colombi, Nathalie Ritter, Diana Weißenberger, Eva Dazert, Mairene Coto-Llerena, Sandro Nuciforo, Lauriane Blukacz, Caner Ercan, Veronica Jimenez, Salvatore Piscuoglio, Fatima Bosch, Luigi M Terracciano, Uwe Sauer, Markus H Heim, Mich
pmc-10642370.description: SummaryMetabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer. However, mechanisms underlying metabolic reprogramming and how altered metabolism in turn enhances tumorigenicity are poorly understood. Here, we report that arginine levels are elevated in murine and patient hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), despite reduced expression of arginine synthesis genes. Tumor cells accumulate high levels of arginine due to increased uptake and reduced arginine-to-polyamine conversion.

pmc-10670731.title: The Dark Side of Multimedia Devices: Negative Consequences for Socioemotional Development in Early Childhood
pmc-10670731.creator: Bruno Rocha, Laura I Ferreira, Cátia Martins, Rita Santos, Cristina Nunes, Pietro Muratori
pmc-10670731.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). There is growing concern about the relationship between screen use by young children and negative effects on their development, as children with developmental and socioemotional impairments tend to have difficulties in their relationships and increased academic problems. The aim of our study was to analyse the relationship between the use of multimedia devices and paediatric symptoms in children below 5 years old. Data from 534 Portuguese parents of children aged from 18 to 57 months were collected via a self-report questionnaire.

pmc-11545050.description: Background/Objectives: Volunteering has been widely recognized as beneficial to the well-being of older adults, providing health benefits, increased social engagement, and a sense of purpose. pmc-12596574.creator: Harmonie Virginie Mangbel’ Ndero
pmc-12596574.description: Although rare, TSH pituitary adenomas are distinguished by their invasive and fibrous appearance. As they are macroadenomas, their total excision is often not possible via the lower approach; the transsphenoidal approach is preferred.ObjectiveTo propose a technique for low endoscopic surgical excision of fibrous adenomas with a greater probability of complete resection.

pmc-12648723.title: Rapid disease progression and hydrocephalus following tarlatamab therapy initiation: A case report
pmc-12648723.creator: Doppo Fukui, Jun Sakakibara-Konishi, Riku Azuma, Yukiko Yoshida, Daisuke Morinaga, Shotaro Ito, Megumi Furuta, Yuta Takasihma, Hidenori Kitai, Satoshi Konno
pmc-12648723.description: Tarlatamab is a novel bispecific T-cell engager immunotherapy that has demonstrated efficacy against small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) in terms of noteworthy anticancer activity and survival outcomes. However, no studies have detailed the patterns of disease progression during tarlatamab treatment. Herein, we present a case of acute disease progression after tarlatamab initiation in a 71-year-old male patient with extensive-stage SCLC.
